articleTitle: Implementation and validation of IED settings in the IEEE 14-Bus System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The article presents and validates a methodology for the parameterization of overcurrent and distance IEDs implemented in four transmission lines of the IEEE 14-bus system. Through simulation in PowerFactory, the pick-up settings and response times for each IED were made and validated. To corroborate the proposed settings, these settings were loaded with real IEDs from the protection laboratory. Finally, the short circuit values were injected using the CMC356 voltage and current injection equipment. The response times of the overcurrent and distance protection functions obtained in simulation have a correlation between 2% and 5% compared to the response times of the real IED and that seen by the CMC356 test set.

articleTitle: A Study on the Comparison and Measurement of Improved CartoonGAN Performance for High-Quality Image Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: With the rapid growth of computer vision, among them, generative artificial intelligence is being used in various industries. CartoonGAN, one of the generating artificial intelligence, can create new images by changing the original image into a cartoon style, which can be used in various fields such as webtoons and animations. To this end, a process of improving the performance of CartoonGAN is necessary, and research for this should be conducted. In this study, to solve the performance degradation that occurs when CartoonGAN is applied, we would like to suggest a direction to improve by applying technologies such as SRCNN and Tiling.

articleTitle: A Privacy-Preserving Smart Body Scale with K-Means Anonymization towards GDPR-Compliant IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: A smart weight scale, or smart scale, is an Internet of Things (IoT)-based scale that can measure metrics other than body weight using various sensors and send the information to the cloud. Meanwhile, the problem is that a person’s weight is considered personally identifiable information (PII) and needs to be preserved to comply with general data protection regulations (GDPR). Our research aim is to use K-Means for anonymization so that a privacy-preserving smart body scale becomes GDPR-compliant. The first step is to form a novel privacy-preserving smart body scale framework. We obtained the cardiovascular disease dataset containing personal weights from Kaggle. We apply random noise perturbation and k-means clustering for anonymization. We apply cardiovascular disease classification using gradient boosting. Finally, we compared the performance of the three anonymization methods with several metrics, including information loss, entropy, and distortion. Test results show that our elbow method shows that the optimum number of clusters for body weight is six. This number has passed the k-anonymity assessment. Furthermore, comparisons show that the k-means generalization performs better than noise perturbation with distortion, information loss, and entropy values 71.1, 0.001, and 15.6, respectively.

articleTitle: Impact of a Weak Grid-network on a Grid-tied Solar Photovoltaic System Supplying a Non-linear Load
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) technology is gaining more attention due to its low maintenance and operation costs. However, a grid-tied solar PV system as well as non-linear loads feed harmonic currents into the grid network, severely affecting the power quality. Recently, studies on power quality issues in grid-tied solar PV systems have been conducted without considering the impact of a grid network quality. A grid network can either be strong or weak, depending on the geographical area. In this study, the impact of a weak grid network on the output performance of a grid-tied solar PV system supplying a non-linear load is investigated. The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) has been used to evaluate the percentage of the total harmonic distortion (THD). The study found that integrating a weak grid network into a solar PV system while supplying a non-linear load, can negatively impact both the current and voltage THD percentages. Hence, it is of great significance to analyze the quality of a grid network before designing a filter to be used to mitigate the harmonics injected by a distributed generation system. As a future study, a filter that can effectively handles a wide range of grid impedance variations needs to be designed.

articleTitle: Visible Light Communication for Outdoor Positioning: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The scope of visible light communication (VLC) in the navigation industry is expanding day by day. This is due to the potential of achieving high navigation accuracy in indoor and outdoor environments. It outperforms the global positioning system (GPS) in providing precise results. In particular, a GPS may not satisfy the stringent need for centimeter-level accuracy. This paper provides a brief review of VLC technology for outdoor navigation. It explores the solid-state lighting technologies that play a pivotal role in achieving accurate localization. It also identifies some emerging areas of applications for VLC-based outdoor positioning systems.

articleTitle: Augmented EEG Signal Classification for Energy Data Visualizations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Classification of electroencephalogram (EEG) data is dependent on data size, quality, and generalizability to decode invaluable information from brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. EEG data collection typically occurs within controlled laboratory environments using long sections. Participation in these experiments draws less attention due to the challenging nature of the EEG experiments and the intended objective. Hence, an approach that offers the potential for both cost and time efficiency is the use of artificial data generation. Data augmentation can improve the classification performance by increasing training data. This study employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) model to enhance the empirically collected EEG dataset, which was introduced for the purpose of analyzing the perceptions of energy users regarding energy data visualizations. The data size is initially expanded through the use of a GAN model. Subsequently, the augmented data is assessed in terms of its classification performance. Three different sample groups—defined as male, female, and mixed—are shown in the results. Each group is used to generate synthetic EEGs, separately. To evaluate the enhanced EEG data, a scenario of transforming EEG data into spectrogram images and then classifying them using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used. The results show that the female sample group performed the best in terms of valence and arousal, with accuracies of 87.9% and 89.06%, respectively. This study shows promising results in terms of increasing EEG data size and improving classification performance.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics of Neurotransmitters and Kirchhoff’s Laws at Neural Synapse
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Since the neural synapse consists in the unstoppable pass of charged electrically neurotransmitters from a neuron to another, then it might be directly explained by the Kirchhoff laws. In this paper, the usage of these laws have yielded a set of equations belonging to classical electrodynamics. Basically, currents and voltages have been derived. Also, it is argued that the synaptic vesicles play the role as capacitors whereas the effect of bunching of neurotransmitters can be see as a type of electrical resistance. The neurotransmitters can create electrical currents so that electrical circuits might be running in the neural synapse. The collapse of these circuits can be perceived as broken of synapse system.

articleTitle: Gender and Race Recognition System with Age Estimation using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Gender, race, and age recognition systems employ machine learning and computer vision techniques to analyze images or video data and provide predictions regarding an individual's gender, race, and age based on their visual characteristics. These systems find extensive utility across various applications, particularly within social media platforms. Gender recognition systems are designed to categorize individuals as either male or female, relying on visual cues extracted from images or videos. Notable visual features used for gender prediction encompass facial characteristics, hairstyle, and attire. Meanwhile, race recognition systems endeavor to discern an individual's racial or ethnic background by analyzing visual traits such as facial features, skin tone, and related attributes. Age recognition systems estimate an individual's age, often within a specified age range, leveraging characteristics like facial wrinkles, skin texture, and hair color. In our research, gender, race and age recognition is carried out by the single model training. A standardized UTK facial image dataset is employed to train our model using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), achieving an approximate model accuracy of 93%.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Charge Storage of Supercapacitor using Parametric Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Supercapacitors, also known as ultracapacitors or electrochemical supercapacitors have emerged as promising energy storage devices due to their high-power density and rapid charge-discharge characteristics. Effective storage of electrical energy is of paramount importance for humans, given its dependence on varied energy sources like hydro, solar, thermal energy, among others. As supercapacitor technology is still in its nascent stage of development, ongoing research in this field holds the promise of positioning supercapacitors as viable contenders for the replacement of conventional batteries in the future. Previous research work has proved that properties of electrode materials used in the construction of supercapacitors play a major role on their performance parameters. The presented research work details use of Response Surface Methodology, a statistical modeling method that describes the unitary and interaction effect of the various electrode material parameters considered for the study. The research presented in this study highlights a significant correlation between the quantity of electrode material applied to the supercapacitor electrodes and their overall performance characteristics. This underscores the crucial role of precise Specific Surface Area loading in enhancing the performance of supercapacitors.

articleTitle: Robust Modified Sorting Weighting CFAR detector for nonhomogeneous Gaussian environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper, we design and analyze the Modified Sorting Weighting (MSW-) Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detector to improve the performance of the convenable conventional ones in homogeneous and nonhomogeneous Gaussian environments. Assuming a Swerling I (SW I) type primary target, closed forms of the detection (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>) and false alarm (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fa</inf>) probabilities of this detector are obtained. Optimum pairs of the weights that guarantee a constant P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fa</inf> and maximize the P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> are also obtained. Conventional CFAR detectors perform well in the homogeneous case or the presence of interference or the clutter edge. Simulation results have shown that this detector exhibits better detection performance and regulation of the P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fa</inf> than the conventional ones in both homogeneous and nonhomogeneous situations.

articleTitle: QHISPIKAY: Military Radio Equipment Defined by Software in the UHF Band for the Peruvian Army
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Radio frequency communication is one of the most important aspects of military operations. These devices allow information to be shared over long distances in a secure and encrypted manner. In developing countries, as is the case of Peru, investment in the acquisition of new military technologies is limited and there is little modern equipment in small quantities. Furthermore, this generates technological dependence within the armed forces, which limits their capacity for development. For this reason, the present work presents the application of the methodology of reverse design to develop a new software-defined UHF military radio equipment. The proposed design has the characteristics of international commercial equipment in terms of range, energy autonomy and military-grade resistance. The developed prototype has been validated to achieve communication of up to 800m, can use up to 16 channels, has autonomy of 3 hours of continuous use and impact resistance of up to 85m in height. The prototype developed has a cost of 400 USD.

articleTitle: Performance Limitation of Utility Scale Battery Storage System: Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The deployment of utility-scale battery storage systems is rapidly expanding to facilitate the seamless integration of renewable energy sources into the electrical grid. However, these systems encounter a range of performance constraints, influenced by factors such as temperature, size, and technological limitations, which can have an impact on their operational efficiency and capacity. To ensure optimal performance of BESS, it is essential to establish a comprehensive understanding of the capabilities and constraints of BESS technology, particularly in areas with environmental conditions resembling to those in Dubai. This paper showcases the complete deployment of a Sodium-Sulfur battery storage system seamlessly integrated into the grid, providing essential support to the Photovoltaic (PV) plant generation in Dubai. The study is focused on evaluating the system’s performance by testing a range of operational conditions and detecting any potential limitations. The findings from these tests have been thoroughly examined and are detailed within this paper.

articleTitle: Training Neural Networks in Cyber-Physical Systems using Design Space Exploration and Co-Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper we present our ongoing research aimed at providing methodologies and tools for reasoning about behavioural properties of AI models in cyber-physical systems. In particular, we envision the use of co-simulation and design space exploration technologies for training ML networks and for validation of the network model for robustness. In detail, we present a simple case study on training a neural network model to approximate the controller action of a thermostat on a room. We show how we can build a training dataset of thousand samples using co-simulation and then using it for training a fully-connected neural network, obtaining ~96% accuracy on testing data. We then show the closed-loop behaviour of the neural model co-simulating it with the controlled system, reporting a mean variation of ∼ 0.3 deg with respect to the nominal controller.

articleTitle: Transmission Loss Reduction in 60 degree Bended Photonic Crystal Waveguide using Polynomial Regression based Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper, polynomial regression based machine learning model is applied to optimize the dielectric rod radius in a 60 degree bended Photonic Crystal (PhC) waveguide for achieving minimum transmission loss throughout the bended waveguide. A feedback based optimization process is proposed to study the electromagnetic transmission loss in a standard PhC model. The simulation results demonstrate a significant 67.79% reduction in transmission loss is achieved through the three stages of optimization compared to the initial unoptimized model, resulting in a transmission efficiency of 98.416%. Later, a comparative analysis of the proposed method and other similar research works revealed that the proposed feedback based method is superior in optimizing a 60 degree bended PhC for reducing electromagnetic transmission loss. A fabrication tolerance study revealed the ability of the proposed model to mitigate the increase in transmission loss due to fabrication inconsistencies.

articleTitle: Business Digital Transformation Strategic Changes During the Covid-19 Pandemic: findings from Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Covid-19 pandemic is over and scholars around the world have been addressing business resilience and preparedness against future emergencies. Digital transformation was a clear response during the epidemic and some changes have remained in today’s business operation. However, it is still unclear how businesses aligned their strategies during the Covid-19 outbreak, especially their digital transformation ones. The aim of this work in progress is to investigate and highlight the business digital transformation strategic changes, which were caused due to the Covid-19 pandemic. This study uses bibliometric analysis to define the effects of Covid-19 outbreak on business digital transformation, while relevant terms are specified and defined.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Cooperative AF-NOMA Networks in Power Line Communication Systems with ISIC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This study delves into the realm of non-orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) Power Line Communication (PLC) networks employing amplify and forward configurations, while considering the incorporation of imperfect Successive Interference Cancellation (ISIC). The focus lies in unveiling a precise closed-form analytical framework for quantifying the outage probability within the NOMA-PLC network, particularly under the influence of ISIC. To counteract the detrimental effects imposed by ISIC on the outage probability of the NOMA-PLC system, this work systematically computes and unveils optimal power allocation factors for NOMA-PLC users. The viability of these analytical findings is corroborated through a series of simulations and numerical analyses, effectively validating the robustness and accuracy of the proposed analytical models.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Rotor Eccentricities in Two-Pole Synchronous Generators By Spectrum Analysis of Complex Split-Phase Currents
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Two-pole synchronous machines (turbogenerators) are high power machines used in generating plants, needing careful monitoring to avoid costly faults. The rotors may fail due to thermal, mechanical, and magnetic problems. Rotor eccentricities make rise unbalances in the stator armature split-phase currents. This paper shows a diagnosis method based on symmetrical components analysis in 2-pole round-rotor machines, and FFT spectral analysis of 4-pole complex sequence currents carried out from split-phase currents. The split-phase current signature analysis is validated in this paper by extensive time-stepping finite-elements simulations of a 600MVA practical turbogenerator, with various fault degrees, voltage levels, and loads. The results show very good agreement between the theoretical previsions and the simulations.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra Low-Power Tunable Ring VCO in 65 nm CMOS Technology for 2.9-4.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The design of a tunable ring voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using TSMC 65 nm CMOS technology and a 1 V power supply is presented. The design consists of three inverter stages and capacitive loads for adjusting the frequency. Capacitive loads are implemented as MOS varactors connected to the output of the inverter stages. It is shown that the resulting design has a power dissipation of 0.65 mW, provides a tunable frequency range from 2.9 GHz to 4.5 GHz for -1.5 V to 1.5 V control voltage and phase noise of -90dBc/Hz is adequate for tuner application. The proposed VCO provides the frequency control in a wide tuning range and to adjust the oscillation amplitude without increasing the power consumption during the tuning.

articleTitle: Implementation of Quantum Cryptography for Securing IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The globe is observing the emergence of the Internet of Things more prominently recognized as IoT. In this day and age, there exist numerous technological apparatuses that possess the capability to be interconnected with the internet and can amass, convey, and receive information concerning the users. This technology endeavors to simplify existence, however, when the users' information is the central concern for IoT operation, it is necessary to adhere to security measures to guarantee privacy and prevent the exploitation of said information. The customary cryptographic algorithms, such as RSA, AES, and DES, may perform adequately with older technologies such as conventional computers or laptops. Nevertheless, contemporary technologies are heading towards quantum computing, and this latter form possesses a processing capability that can effortlessly jeopardize the aforementioned cryptographic algorithms. Therefore, there arises an imperative necessity for a novel and resilient cryptographic algorithm. To put it differently, there is a requirement to devise a fresh algorithm, impervious to quantum computing, that can shield the information from assaults perpetrated utilizing quantum computing. IoT is one of the domains that must ensure the security of the information against malevolent activities. Besides the conventional cryptography that enciphers information into bits, quantum encryption utilizes qubits, specifically photons and photon polarization, to encode data.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Hardware Accelerator with FPU-Based Runge-Kutta Solvers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In several high-speed computer applications, ordinary differential equations (ODEs) are often utilized. Modern CPUs, however, usually offer a modest throughput for these systems. This paper discusses the implemented design and analysis of a hardware accelerator including second-order, third-order, and fourth-order Runge-Kutta ODE solvers for improving the computing speed and accuracy. The implementation of the hardware accelerators has been done using the VHDL programming language and has been deployed on the Zynq ZC702 FPGA evaluation board. A comprehensive comparative analysis of different Runge-Kutta hardware accelerators, highlighting factors including timing performance, hardware resource usage, and the total on-chip power consumption has been given. According to the experimental findings, the fourth-order Runge-Kutta equation has a significant power consumption, rising by an estimated 51.37 percent and 12.445 percent when comparing second-order and third-order Runge-Kutta solvers at a clock rate of 100 MHz, respectively. This study contributes to the enhancement of ODE solutions in high-performance computing applications.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating the Time of Pedestrians Encounter Timing by Measuring Bluetooth Signal Strength with Multiple Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Traffic safety support systems detect and warn of potential accidents by tracking the location of pedestrians and vehicles. However, most pedestrians and vehicles that do not voluntarily provide location information to the systems will not be tracked by the systems. Therefore, to make the system more advanced, it is necessary to acquire the positions of these pedestrians and vehicles and to predict their positions in a few seconds. This challenge can be partially addressed by having pedestrians who participate in the systems detect the passing of pedestrians who are not tracked by the system and report the passing location and time to the systems. The approximate location of untracked pedestrian is the position of the system participant at the time of passage. Therefore, it is important to obtain the time of passage. The purpose of this research is to estimate the time of passing from the Bluetooth RSSI time series data. This paper proposes a machine learning-based method for estimating the time that a pedestrian wearing a Bluetooth receiver at five points on the body passes a pedestrian carrying a Bluetooth beacon.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Ultra Wideband Filter with Three Stopbands for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: With the increased demand for wireless communication systems for unlicensed indoor applications, the FCC in February 2002, allocated unlicensed bands ranging from 3.1 GHZ to 10.6 GHz with fractional bandwidth of about 109 %, because it plays a key role in the radiofrequency (RF) front ends devices and has been widely applied in many other microwave circuits. Targeting the proposed band defined by the FCC for the UWB system, this article presents a UWB bandpass filter with three stop bands for the mitigation of wireless bands that may interfere with the UWB range. For this purpose, two resonators are utilized for the implementation of triple-notched bands. The C-shaped resonator is used for the first notch band creation at 3.4 GHz to suppress the WiMAX signal while the H-shaped resonator is employed in the initial UWB design to introduce the dual notched characteristic at 4.5 GHz and 8.1 GHz to reject the WLAN and Satellite Communication signals. The overall circuit area covered by the proposed design is 30.6 mm × 20 mm or in terms of guided wavelength at the first stopband its size is 0.06 λg × 0.02 λg. The presented structure shows a good return loss under -10 dB over most of the passband and greater than -15 dB for the notched frequency bands. Finally, the filter is simulated and analyzed in HFSS 15.0. All the bands for the rejection of wireless signals are independently controlled which makes this work superior to the rest of the UWB filters presented in the literature.

articleTitle: Synthetic inertia emulation based on synchronous generator model using parametric identification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: As renewable energy sources (RES) generation increases, power system operators face significant challenges in maintaining the reliability and security of the power system. The rise in non-inertial power sources in small isolated power systems leads to dangerously low levels of inertia and a higher probability of detecting the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF). Regulations issued by ENTSO-E aim to provide additional mitigations and requirements for transmission system operators to ensure the stability and reliability of the power system. One approach to addressing the decreasing amount of inertia in the power system is through synthetic inertia. This paper presents a synthetic inertia methodology, allowing the derivation of a transfer function for a low-order synthetic inertia algorithm using the ARMAX parametric identification model. Based on the proposed methodology, a low-order synthetic inertia transfer function was obtained. The algorithm is easy to implement and does not require additional tuning. Furthermore, the synthetic inertia emulated by the algorithm is equivalent to the traditional inertia of synchronous generators and is measured in seconds. The paper also proposes and conducts a comparison of the performance of the resulting synthetic inertia algorithm with the inertia generated by a synchronous generator.

articleTitle: EEG Channel Analysis for Energy Data Visualizations Using GAF Encoding and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a technique used to assess brain activity during cognitive tasks. EEG signals are generated by a variety of sensors, and due to their inherent complexity, analyzing EEGs can be difficult to retrieve task-related information. To improve the performance of EEG applications, selecting useful EEG channels and minimizing irrelevant channel information can improve the quality of analysis and results. This study focuses on the classification performance evaluation of EEG channels. A unique EEG dataset containing EEG signals is used in response to energy data visualization stimuli to capture users' emotions. To analyze valence emotion in data visualizations, EEG signals are transformed into Gramian Angular Fields (GAF) images, and Deep Learning (DL) features retrieved from GAFs using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) -Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) model. To evaluate valence emotion, a boosting classifier is utilized using a DL feature set reduced by a Principal Component Analysis (PCA) approach. The results demonstrate the success of the technique employed to identify the best channels. The F3 channel has the highest accuracy of 99.76%, while the Fp2 channel has a comparable accuracy of 99.52%. Overall, the suggested technique shows promising outcomes in identifying valence emotion for energy data representations.

articleTitle: Conducted Emission Measurements with a CDN Showing Very High-Frequency Component Effects in a Synchronous Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Modern high-frequency power electronic converters consisting of smaller-sized components composing higher switching frequencies are more prone to noise emissions into the Very High Frequency (VHF) band.Pre-compliance conducted emission testing can be performed in the development laboratory with a Line Impedance Stabilising Network (LISN) that can be constructed and calibrated. As most conducted Electro-Magnetic Compatibility (EMC) tests are performed up to 30 MHz, and some only to 10 MHz, conducted noise emissions beyond this band are not intended to be verified with the standard LISN. If the pre-compliance conducted emission design verification performed in the development laboratory can include the higher frequency bands, well within the VHF frequency range, a more thorough pre-compliance verification can be performed in the development laboratory that can show possible radiation effects.In this paper, we investigated replacing the LISN with a Couple-Decouple Network (CDN) for performing VHF-band conducted emission testing, showing VHF power converter noise phenomena. The CDN sensitivity is demonstrated by showing the UHF effects of a toroidal inductor orientation placement in a two-phase buck converter.

articleTitle: Phishing Windows Login Credentials Using HTML Full-page Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Phishing is a type of cyber-attack that aims to steal sensitive information, such as login credentials and financial data, by masquerading as a trustworthy entity in electronic communication. HTML full-page technique is one of the most recent and sophisticated methods used by cyber criminals in phishing attacks. This paper provides an overview of phishing and HTML full-page technique, explores the underlying technology and mechanisms behind the HTML full-page technique, and discusses potential defenses against this type of attack with a focus on phishing Windows login credentials using HTML full-page technique

articleTitle: Instantaneous Interactions Between Nanoparticles and Tumors Dictated by Bayes Theorem
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the process of internalization for nanoparticles that have been sent as part of a scheme of targeted drug delivery. In this manner, it is applied in a straightforward manner the Bayes’s theorem since the conditional probabilistic have been projected to the action of being accepted or rejected by tumor or target. Furthermore, it is proposed the idea that the interaction between nanoparticles and tumor might be dictated by instantaneous contact by which tumor cells allow or rejects the internalization of drug delivery. Thus, the Dirac-Delta function emerge as an artifact that is added to the electric formulation. Finally the Bayes probability is simulated as function of physical observables.

articleTitle: Strengthening Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) against Black Hole Attacks using Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm and Trust Based Reputation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The rapid evolution of digital technology and its integration into networked systems, especially vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs), has escalated concerns about cybersecurity. The potential ramifications of cyber-attacks on these networks are profound, ranging from traffic disruptions to serious threats to human safety. This research highlights the significant vulnerabilities inherent in VANETs, essential to modern transportation infrastructure. The paper focuses on developing robust security strategies and countermeasures to prevent unauthorized network access and to facilitate prompt detection and mitigation of cyber threats in VANETs.

articleTitle: Design of Ku Band High Efficiency 4W Power Amplifier in GaAs pHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper reports a 12-15 GHz 4 W monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) power amplifier (PA) designed in 0.25 µm GaAs pHEMT technology. With the proposed matching method, the two-stage PA achieves a flat small signal gain of 16-17 dB across a wide band. The simulated power-added efficiency (PAE) reaches a peak of 26%. Obtaining the output power (Pout) of 36 dBm at 1 dB compression point (P1dB). Both the input and output Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) values are below 1.33. One of the main goals of the design process is to construct passive circuits that can provide the required broad-frequency, low-loss impedance transformation network.

articleTitle: Innovative Frequency Reconfigurable UWB Antenna Utilizing Metamaterial and DGS Approach for Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to propose a novel frequency-reconfigurable UWB (Ultra-Wideband) antenna by utilizing metamaterials (Split Ring Resonators) and the Defected Ground Structure (DGS) approach for applications in cognitive radio. We commence by designing a UWB antenna that functions at three specific resonant frequencies: 4.81 GHz, 6.12 GHz, and 9.63 GHz, achieving optimal S11 levels at -54.21 dB, -23.91 dB, and -47.88 dB, respectively. This UWB antenna offers a wide bandwidth ranging from 3.95 GHz to 12 GHz, with an average gain of 3 dBi. Following this, we incorporate reconfigurability features to expand the number of resonant frequencies, making it suitable for cognitive radio applications. The results of this study are based on simulations carried out in CST MWS, and we further validate these findings using HFSS software.

articleTitle: Rejection Band Enhancement of Compact Double-Layered Dual Band BPF Using Stepped Impedance DGS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Recently, A design technique of compact dual band bandpass filter is developed using a double-layered technology. To show the potential of this technique and increase the filter capability, the proposed dual band filter is modified with ultra-wide stopband performance in this article. Indeed, a stepped impedance resonator (SIR) is realized and patterned in a DGS closed to the input/output feeding ports. To achieve that properly, the characteristic frequency of the suggested SIR is analyzed using even-odd method and its dimensions are calculated at the unwanted spurious frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>). To improve the above concept, a dual band BPF working at 2.4/3.5 GHz is designed, simulated, and measured for multi-communication system purposes. The filter responses from simulation and measurements are compared and discussed. Consequently, the final modified filter is accomplished with a rejection band performance better than19 dB up to 10 GHz.

articleTitle: A Comparative study on Total Ionizing Dose Effects of 100-V Split-gate Trench VDMOS and Conventional Trench VDMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a comparative study on the effects of Total Ionizing Dose (TID) radiation on the Split-Gate Trench VDMOS (SGT-MOS) and the conventional Trench VDMOS (T-MOS), both with equal rated breakdown voltages of 100 V, using experimental methods. The experimental findings reveal that the same degradation trends in the threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) were found for both types of devices. However, the breakdown voltage (BV) of SGT-MOS exhibits greater sensitivity to TID radiation compared to the T-MOS. Utilizing Sentaurus TCAD, we analyze and discuss the variances in BV shifting behavior between the SGT-MOS and T-MOS. The differences in BV shifting behavior between SGT-MOS and T-MOS can be attributed to the positive oxide trapped charges induced by TID, which could significantly affect the electric field distribution for SGT-MOS, but not for T-MOS. To address this issue, three methods are proposed to enhance the TID tolerance for the SGT-MOS and T-MOS. These methods include avoiding high-temperature processes, reducing the thickness of the oxide layer, and decreasing the doping in the drift layer.

articleTitle: Development of Artificial Intelligence Supported Tool for Anomaly Detection in Cloud Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of Internet of Things (IoT) and Cloud systems, the complexity and scale of these technologies demand innovative solutions for efficient error detection and management. This paper proposes a robust framework for anomaly detection in cloud computing systems, emphasizing the critical role of automation and artificial intelligence (AI). The approach integrates Continuous Integration, Continuous Deployment (CICD) principles with AI-driven anomaly detection techniques to enhance system reliability and minimize risks. The study introduces a novel method employing one-dimensional convolutional layers and Autoencoder architecture to preprocess and analyze system metrics, enabling the development of an adaptive and customized anomaly detection system. The proposed framework is implemented through a Python-based agent, utilizing specific libraries and Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) processes executed via Jenkins. The agent is tested and deployed on Kubernetes, demonstrating its effectiveness in dynamic and complex environments. The results highlight the significance of iterative optimization, emphasizing continuous monitoring and adaptation for ensuring the robustness and reliability of cloud computing systems. This research contributes valuable insights into enhancing the efficiency of anomaly detection in large-scale cloud systems, paving the way for further advancements in the field of IoT and cloud technologies.

articleTitle: Flexible Manufacturing Systems: CAD Programs to Simulate the Movements of Industrial Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Currently, the simulation and programming of industrial robots are carried out using commercial software applications from robot manufacturing companies. These software applications are expensive, and some require installation on robust computing equipment. In this work, the experiences obtained during the Manufacturing Systems Automation course for Mechatronic Engineering students are shared. During this course, different configurations of industrial robots were used, and simulations of the trajectory of the end effector were carried out using a CAD software application aimed at the Academy with free licenses for students. The objective of this implementation was to 1) generate simulation solutions for different configurations of industrial robots through a CAD software application and 2) determine if there was a positive evolution or progress to create said simulation solutions, which were presented with an increasing level of difficulty. Both items were evaluated using a checklist. The results demonstrate that using CAD software applications is an option to generate simulation solutions for the trajectories of industrial robots in an accessible way and that they are digital teaching tools acceptable to students, promoting HumanComputer Interaction.

articleTitle: Computational Analysis of a Serpentine Pulley-Belt System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the serpentine pulley-belt system, which consists of a flexible belt coupled with rigid pulleys. This system has been adequately described by a nonlinear model and linear approximations of it, obtained from systems implemented in physical form. This paper presents computational tools designed for the analysis of: (i) the feasibility of physical realization from a set of proposed parameters and (ii) the parametric dependence of the modes presents in the steady-state response. The computational tools together facilitate mathematical analysis, reduce design time and allow to obtain mathematically and graphically the static response of the system, since they allow to determine a priori the frequency, phase lag and amplitude of the oscillation of the band sections, which significantly helps the analysis and design of the same.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Self-Heating Effect in HEMT Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The analysis of power dissipation and operating temperature is of great importance for electrothermal design in power electronics. In this communication, an electrothermal simulation analysis of AlGaN/GaN double metal gate (DMG) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) using finite element method (FEM) was done. The thermal and electrical behavior of the device was evaluated by simulating the output and transfer characteristics with and without Joule effect and power dissipation. In addition, we have carefully studied the effect of VDS drain polarization on the increase in the HEMT operating temperature. The results indicate that self-heating significantly degrades the electrical performance of the device, as evidenced by the increase in the operating temperature of the transistor.

articleTitle: Stochastic Hybrid Algorithms to Estimate Stroke in Diabetic Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Commonly, stroke is strongly related to those periods by which the patient has surpassed high values of glucose as well as when there is evidence of high cholesterol and blood pressure and others minor causes. While a permanent control inside the allowed ranges at the critic indicators is achieved, then the risk to acquire stroke turns out to be pretty low. In this paper, the theorem of Bayes and the Monte Carlo method are combined to construct a hybrid algorithm that yields the probability of stroke event as function of Bayes prediction and the Monte Carlo steps. The results are strongly depending on the life-style of patient so that the algorithm can be used to explore possible pessimistic scenarios that can be systematically optimized. From results of this paper, an event of stroke might emerge from a few Monte Carlo steps with a high Bayesian probability, fact that turns out to be highly dependent on conditions and history of patient more than random sequences.

articleTitle: CyberSafe: A Gamified Cyber Security Training Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper, we address the growing concern of cyberattacks due to low awareness among computer users. Many organizations have started implementing workshops and training programs to educate their employees and users about cybersecurity. However, some of these programs lack sufficient knowledge and fail to engage participants effectively. To overcome these limitations, we present a novel system called CyberSafe, developed using the Unity game engine. CyberSafe comprises multiple levels of training, each focusing on an important aspect of cybersecurity that users commonly encounter in their daily lives. A player can choose one of these levels and follow Nova AI’s instructions. By providing a hands-on learning experience, CyberSafe aims to increase users’ awareness and equip them with the necessary skills to navigate the internet safely and mitigate the risk of falling victim to cyberattacks. We conducted pre- and post-tests with users who interacted with the CyberSafe system, and the results demonstrate a significant improvement in their awareness and ability to detect different types of attacks. Moreover, the CyberSafe system offers a flexible, user-friendly, and enjoyable approach to enhancing knowledge about cyberattacks.

articleTitle: Study of quantum algorithms and their implementations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this work, we studied some quantum algorithms, and selected Grover search problem, it will then receive an in-depth analysis of how the problem works and how it can be adapted to its process in a quantum computer, and a quantum solution using python qiskit library will be elaborated.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network-Based Protection Algorithm for Transmission Lines Connecting DFIG-Based Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper discusses the challenges faced by conventional distance relay in protecting lines emanating from doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind farms. During severe faults, the fundamental component of the short circuit current of DFIG is no longer at the system nominal frequency. Besides, the short circuit current rapidly decays to low values shortly after the fault. This behavior may result in incorrect operation of the distance relay, which is configured assuming that the electrical grid is powered only by synchronous generators. Furthermore, an artificial neural network (ANN)-based protection algorithm is proposed for comprehensive fault detection and isolation. The proposed algorithm employs maximal overlap discrete Wavelet Transform to analyze the fault signals. Only local current and voltage measurements are used in the tripping decision; therefore, eliminating the need of a communication link with the other end of the line. To train the ANNs, simulation was carried out including a wide set of system operating conditions. The results were promising, where the proposed algorithm was able to detect and locate all types of faults when the line is connected to a DFIG-based wind farm, regardless of the prevailing system conditions.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration of Uganda’s HV and associated MV network to manage fault levels attached to accelerated power generation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The rapid expansion of power generation in Uganda signals economic growth but presents challenges in high-voltage (HV) and medium-voltage (MV) networks due to increased fault levels. This study analyzes fault levels in Uganda’s transmission network, emphasizing the correlation between increased power generation and its direct impact on network fault levels. To address these problems, the proposed reconfiguration of the HV network is proposed. Findings reveal a substantial increase in fault levels across various network buses, particularly at Lira and Opuyo, with fault currents rising by a range of 40% to 250%. Lira experiences an increase from 0.8 kA to 27 kA, and Opuyo from 1.03 kA to 30.7 kA. Buses like Nalubaale/Kira and UETCL Iganga approach the recommended fault level threshold of 80%. To ensure the reliability of the network, it is recommended to upgrade capacity and improve equipment at key substations. A detailed cost-benefit analysis shows the possibility of annual savings of up to USD 390 million if the proposed network changes and improvements are addressed.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of CO2 emission in Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In recent times, there has been a drive towards just energy transition. Developing countries such as South Africa, have found themselves at the forefront of this move. However, it is not apparent that the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission profiles have been taken into consideration as the policies were being developed. As a result, this paper investigates the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission profiles per annum, per capita, by sector and by energy source for Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. Evidently, these countries have significant differences in populations. However, Nigeria and Kenya show similarities in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, particularly in transportation sector. These could enable such countries to share knowledge in the development of policies to reduce the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions by the transportation sector. Nevertheless, these countries are dependent on fossil fuels for their energy needs. Transition to renewable energy sources in these countries can have a significant impact on their drive to reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions.

Author Keywords: CO2 emissions per unit of GDP

articleTitle: Hardware-in-the-Loop System of the Autonomous Municipal Cleaning Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Autonomous municipal cleaning vehicles consist of a number of subsystems, and the most important for autonomy are the driving subsystem, the perception subsystem, and the cleaning subsystem. To prepare control algorithms for the real vehicle, all three subsystems must be functional. Simulation environments that simulate the driving subsystem already exist. The perception subsystem can be simulated to some extent, but its preparation can also be done by previously recorded information from non-autonomous vehicles. The control of cleaning subsystem is not easy to simulate. For this reason, in this paper, we present a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) system for controlling the autonomous municipal cleaning vehicle, combining the rig of the real cleaning system with the simulation of vehicle motion and perception, which is the main contribution of this paper. We present the developed HIL system and the results of several experiments during the testing of the system.

articleTitle: A Rapid and Simple Method for Prostate Cancer Detection Using an Electronic Tongue from Patients in Urine Samples
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This work describes a simple and rapid method to detect a group of patients with prostate cancer from the acquisition of urine samples by implementing an electronic tongue composed of screen-printed carbon electrodes (C110). To validate the detection of prostate cancer samples, other samples were acquired from a group of patients called controls (i.e., healthy patients, patients with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia and Prostatitis), which were subsequently classified using Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning methods. The results achieved were outstanding since it was possible to obtain up to 92.9% in the sample's classification accuracy.

articleTitle: The Stroke Event as a Shannon Entropy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The event of stroke is seen as a confluence of various anomalies, particularly in diabetic patients. Thus, the random confluence can also be perceived as a disorder of system that might be dictated by the Shannon entropy. In this paper, the idea that stroke is a manifestation of entropy is studied. Basically, the variables that would trigger the event are classified as the causes of disorder of system. Thus, stroke becomes a function as weight of variables. These are mainly glucose, blood pressure, cholesterol, BMI, etc. Numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Regulation of Hybrid Marine Microgrid System Employing Improved TIDF Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a competent approach for controlling load frequency (LFC) in a hybrid maritime microgrid system (HMGS). This microgrid system comprises of a marine biodiesel generator (BDG), solid oxide fuel cell, wind turbine generator (WTG), renewable energy sources (RESs), Tidal power generation (TPG), both sensitive and non- sensitive loads. A trustworthy metaheuristic optimization approach known as honey badger algorithm (HBA)is used to adjust the settings of the proposed I-TDF controller. Comparative evaluations of various controllers reported in the past study highlight the remarkable performance of the intended I-TDF controller, which includes TIDF and PIDF controllers. Finally, simulation results obtained with MATLAB software confirm the usefulness and dependability of the proposed I-TDF controller. The intended controller can provide system stability while lowering overshoot and shortening the system's settling and rising durations.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Accessibility of Banking Web Sites in Malaysia Using Wave
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: E-banking has become a key service, allowing users to carry out financial transactions without the need for a physical presence. However, with over 1.8% of Malaysia’s population suffering from disabilities, maintaining web accessibility for e-banking platforms is critical. To uncover accessibility concerns, this study conducted a detailed examination of the selected e-banking websites in Malaysia. The accessibility evaluation in this study focused on the homepage of selected e-banking web page since it is considered the most crucial page as it plays a significant role in shaping the initial perception of web users. Using the WAVE automated tool, considerable differences in accessibility problems were discovered among the top five banks in Malaysia, with issues ranging from contrast faults to missing alternate texts and empty navigational components. The analysis underlines the importance of consistent online banking accessibility standards and the importance of fixing these challenges for an inclusive digital banking experience. The study emphasizes the necessity of making e-banking platforms accessible to everyone, reinforcing the need for stringent web design standards in the financial sector.

articleTitle: Highly Linear and Efficient Power Amplifier using Wideband Modulated Matching Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: High linearity and efficiency are key characteristics of power amplifiers especially in 5G and WiFi6 applications. Envelope tracking and Doherty Power Amplifiers (DPA) show excellent efficiency numbers but have limitations in linearity or achievable bandwidth. This paper proposes a new design approach using modulated matching that achieves excellent efficiency and linearity at the same time making it an ideal candidate for 5G and WiFi6 power amplifier designs. Transistor level simulations indicate that efficiencies of 32% with -30dB of EVM are achievable for WIFI 6 MCS7 (MCS= Modulation Coding Scheme) conditions. For higher data rate conditions like MCS9 the proposed design meets -35dB of EVM with an efficiency of 26%. For 5G band N41 (2.5GHz) applications simulations show efficiencies of 45% with ACLR values <38dBc for modulation bandwidths up to 100MHz.

articleTitle: Dual-MIC Delay Matching for Adaptive Noise Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a new adaptive noise cancellation algorithm designed to improve speech quality in noisy environments. Background noise often degrades the quality of voice signals in various applications, such as online meetings and voice recognition. Since the performance of the adaptive noise cancellation degrades when the bandwidth of the noise is large. The proposed algorithm adopts a delay-matching method to synchronize the noise received from multiple microphones. The delay-matching minimizes the phase difference between the desired signal and the noise. The results show that our algorithm outperforms existing adaptive noise cancellation methods regarding noise removal performance. The ability to adapt to large spectrum noise and maintain high speech quality highlights its potential to transform the user experience in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Towards an Environmentally-friendly Street Sweeping Vehicle with Reduced Water Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Cities and municipalities that have organized intensive cleaning of streets and public areas provide their residents with better and healthier living conditions. Regular cleaning with a fleet of cleaning vehicles has both positive and negative effects, as the vehicles contribute to a significant increase in the concentration of PM10 particles in the air and, to a lesser extent, PM2.5 particles due to the dust raised by the cleaning vehicle on the road. This paper describes the development of a wet cleaning control subsystem installed on an all-electric cleaning vehicle to minimize the increase in the concentration of PM2.5 and PM10 particles. The experimental results of PM measurement during the cleaning operations of the vehicle show that the installation position of the PM sensors plays a key role in the successful control of dust suppression.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Inspired Antenna Array for Next-Generation 5G Wireless Systems and Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper investigates the design of a double-sided 1×4 linear hexagonal bowtie antenna array based on the complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR) configuration. The CSRR integrated into the hexagonal patches on both layers develops metamaterial (MTM) properties, enhancing the antenna's performance. Simulated results show resonance at 3.5GHz with a return loss below -10dB between 3.15GHz to 4.5GHz. The E-Plane and H-plane radiation patterns at 3.5GHz demonstrate gains of 8.5dBi and 8dBi, respectively. The improved gain and wideband characteristic of the proposed antenna make it suitable for 5G and Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication applications. The 3D radiation pattern further illustrates the antenna array's capabilities.

articleTitle: Towards more reliable community load profiling for future renewable energy projects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In South Africa, a significant rural population lacks electricity access, hindering economic development. Although microgrids have shown potential to alleviate this, these systems mainly serve urban areas, leaving rural communities underserved. This is mainly due to unreliable load profiling in rural areas, which does not boost investor confidence. In this paper, a reliable load profiling of a rural area in South Africa is put forward. Historical electricity consumption data was collected from three feeders supplying the Nduma district and processed to identify consumption patterns and trends. Results showed a significant impact of Covid-19 restrictions and load-shedding on the overall load profile.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hydroponic Cultivation Kit with IoT for Edible Flowers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Edible flowers have recently become popular. When cultivating them in soil, we need special attention to issues such as pests, diseases, and chemical fertilizers. Also, as the cultivation process demands significant effort, often relying on experience and intuition, it will be difficult, especially for beginners. We want everyone to be able to grow them effortlessly and enjoyably. We then aim to support edible flower cultivation using IoT and AI technologies. In this paper, we design and implement a hydroponic cultivation kit with IoT as a first step. The cultivation kit possesses sensing data collection, monitoring and recording, and notification functions to support the cultivation. Through the prototype system, the functions showed that it has the potential to provide cultivation support and enjoyment.

articleTitle: An evaluation of the viability of using renewable energy sources to power a sizable hotel in Salalah, Oman
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Paper examines the potential for a large-scale tourist operation in Salalah to run on renewable energy sources (RES) independently. The analysis makes use of data on electrical consumption from a hotel. The analysis uses the net present cost and the cost of energy as evaluation criteria This research compares diesel standalone generator, RES, and hybrid technologies using RES assessment software tools, HOMER (National Renewable Energy Laboratory), and found that while the standalone generator has net present cost and cost of energy of $ 2263420 and $0.4756, the renewable energy and hybrid energy systems have $1909726, $2690442 and $0.4011, $0.5762 respectively, making the renewable energy system to be most cost effective in providing energy for the hotel in Salalah. The modeling results show that RES has the potential to meet the power needs of large-scale tourist accommodation in principle. Optimal simulations show that renewable energy sources alone can meet all of the nation's electricity needs. The results of the modeling and analysis show that RES can be a practical and cost-effective alternative to the traditional fossil fuel power generator set currently used by major tourist operations.

articleTitle: Rethinking False Positives with Class Activation Maps: Can we define false positives without ground-truths?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this study, we have used Class Activation Mapping (CAM) technique to improve the accuracy of our Gloves classification model. By extracting the CAM and computing its areas, we have created a mechanism that effectively reduces false positives. We have trained the ResNet18 model on 2000 images of hands with and without gloves, achieving 98.65% accuracy. We have used the last convolutional layer of the model to extract the CAM outputs using the Gradient-CAM technique. Then, we have taken the extracted areas into account to decide whether a hand exists in the given image. Our results show that this approach is effective in reducing false positive detections.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Single Phase GaN Half Bridge Inverter for Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This paper presents a design and hardware implementation of a gallium nitride (GaN) single-phase inverter to be used in the photovoltaic system instead of a silicom (SI) single-phase inverter. GaN inverters are evaluated in terms of their switching losses, efficiency, and total harmonic distortion. GaN inverters also have a higher switching frequency and faster switching speeds, which can further improve the efficiency of the inverter system. The results show that the GaN inverter has lower switching losses and higher efficiency compared to the Si inverter. The paper concludes that GaN inverters are a promising alternative and have several advantages over silicon (Si) inverters for power conversion.

articleTitle: Python script to recognize user gestures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The study presents the research and development of a Python script that uses a computer webcam to recognize hand gestures and mimic mouse movements in offline window management and in online document navigation. Its purpose is to make the computer easier to use for people with limited physical abilities by providing a new, natural and convenient way to interact with the computer system. In designing the current gesture recognition tool, a hybrid approach based on the optical principle, marker-based by extracting spatial features of hand joint positions, and a specially designed algorithm for initialization, tracking, recognition and real-time processing of pre-entered gesture patterns for the left and right hand. The chosen approach does not rely on large-scale repositories of digital images, does not segment objects from the image background, has no requirements, and is not affected by environmental factors. The gesture recognition script was tested in different environments - online and locally on a Windows operating system. Performed tests and experiments prove that the application accurately recognizes gestures and imitates mouse movements.

articleTitle: New Radio Polar Coding Performance Enhancement Study Using QAM and APSK Modulation Schemes for 6G
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In various regions of the world, the 5G network has been operational since 2020. In 5G better spectrum and power resources are included as extra features. A better network is still required, nevertheless, to support the Internet of Everything and the needs of the holographic society. Consequently, it is anticipated that the 6G network will debut in 2030 to meet future demand. The new 6G technologies will improve the air interface and transmission technologies. Enhanced channel coding is one of these new technologies. For 5G, the 3GPP chose the channel coding techniques to be LDPC and Polar codes. By enhancing the 5G polar codes performance it can be applied as channel coding techniques in 6G. Using higher-order modulation techniques with these polar codes is one approach. We have used polar codes with 16APSK and QAM with low code rates to improve the performance of 5G polar codes. The result showed better BER performance for polar codes with 16APSK and QAM at a low coding rate than BPSK modulation with a high code rate.

articleTitle: Vegetation Path Loss Modeling Using a Modified Parabolic Equation Toolbox
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of modelling radio wave propagation through vegetation using parabolic equation methods is investigated by modifying the parabolic equation toolbox (PETOOL) to incorporate a mechanism to model vegetation. The vegetation was modeled as a lossy dielectric slab. The geometry of the problem was configured as a stratified three-layer homogeneous medium model (air, vegetation, and ground) with each layer modeled by its dielectric properties (permittivity and conductivity). The discrete mixed Fourier transform was used to propagate the radio wave through the lossy dielectric slab. To evaluate the model, a scenario with the both transmitter and receiver antennas located inside the vegetation canopy was configured as a simulation setup, and the results compared to the well known results by Tamir. The result of interest from the model was the propagation path loss of radio waves in the presence of vegetation. To assess agreement between the modified PETOOL and Tamir’s results, the root mean square error between the results was calculated. It was found that as the imaginary component of the complex refractive index approaches zero, the solution to the discrete mixed Fourier transform, for which the propagation calculation is based, becomes unstable leading to failed agreement with Tamir’s results.

articleTitle: A Study on High-Quality Style Transfer Using Edge-Enhanced Gaussian Smoothing Technique(EEGST) for Minimizing Perceptual Loss
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Recent advancements in image generation technologies, particularly those involving style transfer, have garnered significant attention. Style transfer involves merging the characteristics of one stylistic image with the content of another to produce a novel image. Most image generation techniques, including style transfer, heavily rely on neural networks. However, the use of neural networks, particularly during processes such as up-sampling, can introduce artifacts. This paper proposes a method to mitigate artifacts in models utilizing neural networks, specifically focusing on the style transfer model proposed in "Perceptual Losses for Real-Time Style Transfer and SuperResolution" [5]. The mentioned model exhibits advantages in terms of speed but suffers from checkerboard artifacts or similar issues. The proposed approach effectively addresses these concerns, reducing artifacts while preserving the overall form of the image. The method involves combining Gaussian smoothing to handle artifacts introduced by neural networks while ensuring the preservation of edges. The simplicity and versatility of the proposed method make it applicable to various models. This paper presents a method to reduce artifacts in neural networkbased models, with a particular focus on the style transfer model benchmarked against "Perceptual Losses for Real-Time Style Transfer and Super-Resolution." The proposed approach proves effective in maintaining image structure while mitigating artifacts, showcasing its potential applicability across different models.

articleTitle: CADS: Cyber-Attack Detection System Using Decision Tree for Automotive Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Modern vehicles are equipped with a large number of electronic control units (ECUs) to provide more convenient and safe services for drivers. These ECUs are required to share the various control data for driving using the CAN (Controller Area Network) protocol that is one of the communication protocols for in-vehicle networks. Recently, as vehicles become capable of real-time, two-way communication with various elements on the road, modern vehicles faces a wide range of security issues. The in-vehicle networks are already suffered from the cyber-attacks exploiting newly exposed security vulnerabilities. However, it cannot guarantee the safety and security of the vehicles from as the CAN is designed without considering security. Therefore, this paper proposes a machine learning-based cyber-attack detection system (CADS) in CAN to ensure driving safety. This CADS learns the data pattern of the CAN frames generated while the driving and is able to distinguish between regular messages and cyberattack messages. The performance of the fully trained detection model of the CADS is evaluated using a vast number of testing dataset. The results show that our CADS in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score has 100% of the detection rate for regular messages, replay attacks, brute-force attacks except for modification messages.

articleTitle: Investigation of Wireless Power Transfer Based on the Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: Electricity generation and distribution are both processes that have become an essential part of human existence, and so, to ensure the continued use of these processes, more sustainable alternatives must be investigated, the use of renewable energy sources such as solar energy, wind energy, and hydropower have mitigated this problem but have not solved it entirely, as they have only addressed the sustainability issue with electricity generation and not transmission, which is what this document addresses with the investigation and use of the alternative method of electricity distribution: wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: HardnessTesterV: A Web Machine Learning application for Vickers Hardness Prediction of a Metallic Alloy Using Flask API
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: This research presents the HardnessTesterV app- a web application for predicting the Vicker hardness of Laser welded Metallic alloy using Flask API, HTML, and CSS to build the front end and back end. Vickers hardness is an important property in the manufacturing industry, and predicting it accurately is vital for material selection and design. The Web application takes some of the important processing parameters as the input features and uses a random forest Machine learning model to predict its Vickers hardness. Flask API was used to create a RESTful interface that provides a user-friendly platform for users to submit the combinations of the processing parameters and receive predictions. HTML and CSS were used to design the front end of the web application to provide a visually appealing interface for users. The application was deployed on a PythonAnywhere cloud server, making it easily accessible to users. The application was deployed on a cloud server, making it easily accessible to users worldwide. The accuracy of the predictions was evaluated using various metrics and the results showed that the developed model can accurately predict the Vickers hardness of metallic alloys. HardnessTesterV web app measures the Vickers hardness of 2507 Duplex stainless steel material. The web application is expected to be a valuable tool for engineers and researchers in the manufacturing industry for material selection and design.

articleTitle: Security risk assessment of electricity supply at 400/220/110/20 kV Urechesti power substation from Romania
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical, Communication and Computer Engineering (ICECCE)
abstract: The assessment of the security risk of electricity supply to industrial and household consumers within the National Power System, comes in the context in which the possibility of a black-out is very likely, and the lack of electricity can cause major damage through enormous financial losses, which through the domino effect can spread economic and national insecurity. In this context, the risk assessment of the security of electricity supply to industrial consumers becomes an essential issue of national security and makes this paper of real interest. As known in the literature, the 400 kV and 220 kV power substations within the National Power Grid Transelectrica, are listed as critical energy infrastructures and for this reason this paper requires essential multidisciplinary, interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary knowledge of power engineering, industrial engineering, security and protection of critical power infrastructures and energy security. The essential and interesting elements brought in this risk analysis are: determining the probability of the chosen risk scenario, determining the severity, calculation of the risk matrix and elaboration of the energy security strategy on the power substation in this paper. The authors consider that the security of electricity supply to consumers within the National Power System is a strictly national and european security issue because the lack of electricity can cause enormous damage to the industry, economy and state systems, which are almost entirely dependent on electricity.
